stories.desc: From colorful orbs to delicate spirals, heating and manipulating glass allows artists to create beautiful translucent sculptures.

stories.title: Optical experiment demonstrates the strong Mpemba effect in a single qubit
stories.desc: Typically, after a physical system is disturbed, it can gradually return toward a state of thermal equilibrium by exchanging heat with its surroundings. Thermal equilibrium is a state in which there is no net transfer of heat between the system and its surroundings.

stories.title: A Strange Quantum Theorem Has Killed Einstein’s Reality
stories.desc: Albert Einstein fought to save our everyday notion of reality from the strangeness of quantum mechanics. But those who set out to aid him keep poking holes in his argument. The post A Strange Quantum Theorem Has Killed Einstein’s Reality first appeared on Quanta Magazine

stories.title: Why Brittle Solids Crack Under Pressure
stories.desc: Author(s): Ryan Wilkinson Theory and experiments suggest that the mysterious fractures that appear when a brittle material is compressed result from a hidden buildup of internal tension. [Physics 19, 151] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026

stories.title: Record-low temperature created on China’s space station
stories.desc: With gravity's effects mitigated, atoms orbiting Earth on China’s space station reached about 10 trillionths of a kelvin.

stories.title: Rising cost of living tests UK's net zero ambitions
stories.desc: From floods to wildfires to heatwaves, 2026 is the year it became hard to ignore the impact of climate change on UK weather. But will soaring living costs affect the government’s commitment to tackling climate change?

stories.title: Two paths, one flux: Trapped ions simulate Aharonov–Bohm interference in a lattice gauge theory
stories.desc: In a new Nature Physics study, researchers demonstrated the Aharonov-Bohm effect in a quantum simulation of a lattice gauge theory using a hybrid trapped-ion quantum computer.

stories.title: How space weather powers auroras in the sky and threatens power grids on the ground
stories.desc: An aurora is one of nature's most spectacular light shows: It looks like green or red curtains rippling across the night sky. When viewed from the ground, this colorful display might seem far away and disconnected from anything happening on Earth's surface.

stories.title: A Metal with Two Heat Carriers

stories.title: From chaos to 'intelligent' soft matter—how tiny chemical differences guide droplets into ordered structures
stories.desc: Disorder can make sense, and understanding its logic can be genuinely useful. A study by a research group at the University of Trento shows how a minimal chemical difference can turn chaotic, disordered motion into a highly coordinated and reproducible structure.
